workload: soak.js for 3600s: setTimeout(0) churn + self-cancelling intervals + loopback fetch every 4th iter; RSS sampled every 60s
caveats: RSS sampled via ps once/min — coarse, drift is the signal not the level
interval churn reschedules continuously; a cancel-path leak shows as pending growth in last_status
finding: No leak. pending_timers was 9 at minute 1 and 9 at hour 1 across 1,558,920 iterations (1.57M interval fires, 389,730 fetches, 0 errors) — retained work is fully recycled. RSS grew +52MB total but the shape is allocator behavior, not a slope: flat ~30MB for 15min, one step to ~88MB at t=960s (heap resize), flat ~87MB for 35min including a visible GC dip to 59MB at t=1920s, then a step DOWN to ~82MB for the final 7min. A leak climbs; this plateaus.
